summary: PR2 CUTOVER (final teardown, owner ruling 2026-07-21): the drop-history cutover MARKER + the legacy-write FENCE on chat_threads, plus the operator-upgrade halves of the structured assistant-thread ownership/ordering columns (cinatra#1037 P5.6 drop-history, PR2). PR1 (core__0061) added durable per-turn content + structured pause state; PR2 stage-1 added the structured ownership/ordering axes to the BOOTSTRAP DDL (assistant-thread-schema.ts: project_id / team_id / scalars / ordinal + the two partial ownership indexes) and cut the /chat READ path over to reconstruct from the structured store; the final teardown DROPPED the legacy chat_threads INSERT (the structured mirror is now the SOLE authoritative writer), retired the broad chat_thread_* MCP tools + the chat_thread_update project-move UPDATE, and re-pointed every reader onto the structured store. This migration carries three things onto the operator upgrade path: (1) OPERATOR HALVES of the structured columns the bootstrap DDL already provisions on a fresh install — a deployed DB that already has assistant_threads/assistant_turns gains project_id, team_id, scalars (+ object CHECK), ordinal, and the two PARTIAL ownership indexes (assistant_threads_project_updated_idx, assistant_threads_team_updated_idx); every statement idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS / add-constraint-if-absent / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS), a no-op on a bootstrap-produced fresh schema; (2) the cutover MARKER, a singleton table assistant_cutover_marker whose PRESENCE (one row) means 'the drop-history cutover has happened; the legacy chat_threads write path is retired' — this migration SETS the marker row (idempotent INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), because the write surface is provably chat_threads-clean; chat_threads itself is dropped in PR3; a DB-observable marker (not app state) is the Fork-B design source of truth for 'cutover done'; (3) the legacy-write FENCE, a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on chat_threads that RAISEs while the marker exists — Postgres cannot prove app code stopped WRITING chat_threads, so this trigger PROVES it: with the marker now SET, any stray legacy chat_threads INSERT/UPDATE is rejected at the database (DELETE is permitted so the residual-row cleanup path survives). chat_threads is NOT dropped here (PR3) — it is FENCED. Adding+activating this migration is GREEN against the cutover code: NO product path performs a fenced chat_threads INSERT/UPDATE (the writer emits only structured-store queries; project-move types exclude chat_threads; the sole remaining chat_threads operations are DELETEs). GUARDED / IDEMPOTENT (core__0060 + core__0034 pattern): unqualified names ride the runner's search_path (the app schema); the marker table is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; constraints added only when absent (pg_constraint lookup against current_schema()); the fence is CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION + DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS then CREATE TRIGGER; the fence function body looks the marker up in the SAME schema as the fenced table via a dynamic format('… FROM %I.assistant_cutover_marker', TG_TABLE_SCHEMA) — the fired table's schema, NOT an unqualified session-search_path lookup (the app writes chat_threads fully schema-qualified and sets no search_path); the function text is identical to the bootstrap DDL copy in drizzle-store.ts, so operator and fresh installs converge on the same fence — a fresh install is BORN-CUTOVER with the marker set. down() is a STRUCTURAL reverse only (drop the trigger + fence function, the marker table incl. its activation row, the two ownership indexes, and the operator-half columns + scalars CHECK): a migrate-down BEFORE any post-cutover write is clean, but POST-CUTOVER it is LOSSY — the structured columns are now the AUTHORITATIVE ownership/ordering metadata and chat_threads is fenced/no-longer-dual-written, so dropping them discards authoritative metadata with no legacy copy. down() is therefore a DEV/TEST + pre-write operator reverse, NOT a production rollback path once the cutover is live (a live rollback must first re-hydrate chat_threads from the structured store). up() is ADDITIVE (nullable columns + a new singleton table with one activation row + a trigger; no existing data rewritten, no NOT NULL on existing data, no retype, no DROP) — no artifact is REQUIRED; shipped anyway (core__0037/0047/0055/0057/0061 precedent) to keep the fresh-bootstrap and operator-upgrade paths in lockstep with the idempotent buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries mirror (assistantThreadSchemaQueries + the marker/fence/activation copy in drizzle-store.ts). SEQ RENUMBERED AT ROUTE: PR #1915 (assistants W1 registry foundation) merged as core__0065 (squash a508855e), making it the shipped max on origin/main; this migration was therefore renumbered core__0065 -> core__0066 to stay strictly monotonic past the shipped max (rename-only, zero SQL/DDL change). (An earlier route had bumped it core__0063 -> core__0065 while #1915 was still open; once #1915 landed core__0065 the collision forced this second bump to core__0066.) migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
